title: What do the oranges cost, and do zeros matter?
description: Oranges cost fifty six point five zero rupees a kilogram, and the price of two point two five zero kilograms is found by taking away the points and counting digits, the same way as the example in the book. The zeros at the end are then compared.
teaching_notes: One idea: zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value, so they can be dropped before multiplying. Watch for students who think the zeros change the product.

source: The price of 1 kg of oranges is ₹56.50. What is the price of 2.250 kg of oranges? Can we write 56.50 as 56.5 and 2.250 as 2.25 and multiply? Will we get the same product? Why?
video_script.why: The child has seen that the digits after the point in a product come from the two numbers and now meets zeros at the end of a decimal.
video_script.substitution: the book's oranges at fifty six point five zero rupees a kilogram, two point two five zero kilograms
video_script.anchor: Oranges at fifty six rupees fifty paisa a kilogram, and two point two five zero kilograms of them
video_script.payoff_line: The cost of the oranges is now known.

final_answer.value: ₹127.125; yes, the product is the same
final_answer.spoken: one hundred and twenty seven point one two five rupees. Yes, the product is the same

maths_rules: 56.50 = 56.5 since 50 hundredths = 5 tenths; 2.250 = 2.25 since 250 thousandths = 25 hundredths
with the zeros: 5650 × 2250 = 12712500; digits after the point 2 + 3 = 5; 127.12500 = 127.125
size check: 56.5 × 2 = 113 and 56.5 × 3 = 169.5; 2.25 lies between 2 and 3, so the cost lies between 113 and 169.5
zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value
video_script.design: One idea: zeros at the end of a decimal add nothing, so the product is the same with or without them. Assumes the digit rule. The oranges and the weight stay all video; the cost appears only on the answer beat.
